prose:
Techmeme attributes to Alexandr Wang the view that a reported Riemann Hypothesis proof signals that AI will exceed human performance in every field, including AI research, alongside a call for safety and alignment. That is a broad extrapolation from a claimed mathematical development, not evidence that the extrapolation is already true.

The supplied link opens Wang's profile rather than a specific dated statement; the retrieved profile text did not expose the cited post. The argument is therefore summarized only from the feed excerpt. The feed excerpt did not independently establish correctness or the claimed generality; later proof-verification evidence is recorded in the dated update below. This statement must remain distinct from the Masullo formalization dashboard, the Alpöge commentary and the earlier hypothetical interview video.

Verification chronology: the joint Lean FRO/Mathlib certification and MIT register strengthened the evidence on 23 November, when two checks were still pending. Current status, 24 November at 05:25 UTC: [Andrew Sutherland's MIT register](https://math.mit.edu/~drew/grh/) reports that the default-settings paranoid kernel has accepted the export; only one end-to-end lake comparator run remains in progress, in its final Lean default-kernel stage. The earlier two-pending count is historical, not the current state. This source-reported verification is not a build performed for this wiki. It does not validate Wang's all-fields extrapolation or resolve the distinct Masullo manuscript. The register's GRH scope is Dirichlet L-functions. See [the verification report](../summaries/2eaf0b77a9a5.md).
highlights: The statement is attributed to Wang by Techmeme
It extrapolates from a reported mathematical claim to all fields
It also calls for safety and alignment
The source URL is a profile, not a resolved individual post
Retrieved profile content did not contain the cited statement
Later proof certification does not establish the cross-domain extrapolation
As of 24 November 05:25 UTC, one end-to-end comparator run remains pending
